tonight.headline: Your defence slot is still empty — and the defence this afternoon's brief chose just lost two starters
body: Week 3 has not started. ESPN has you at 126.7 projected against Footballers' 120.1, a 53% win probability — and that number already counts a zero at D/ST, because there is nobody in the slot.

This afternoon's card said add the Bengals. Since then Cincinnati's Wednesday report ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill, which is exactly the condition the card said would make it wrong. The card is now the Lions, same drop. Everything else in the lineup is already the projection lineup.

case.label: What the file says
case.body: Fourteen players, nine starting slots, one of them empty. ESPN projects the best free-agent defence at 7.8. Your margin over Footballers is 6.6 before that is filled.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Footballers start Matthew Stafford because Caleb Williams is listed doubtful, and Brock Bowers and Malik Nabers are both questionable. If Bowers plays a full game, their tight end outscores yours by about two points, which is inside your margin only if the defence slot is filled.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Footballers pick up a healthy quarterback or both Bowers and Nabers clear Friday with full practices — then the matchup is a genuine coin flip and the defence becomes the deciding seat rather than a cushion.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Detroit kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Add the Lions D/ST, drop Jonah Coleman
doFirst.subtitle: Free agent, no priority spent. It replaces a guaranteed zero — and replaces this afternoon's Bengals pick, which lost two defensive tackles on Wednesday's report.

case.label: Why not the Bengals any more
case.body: CBS Sports' Week 3 report lists Cincinnati DTs Jonathan Allen (knee) and B.J. Hill (Achilles) out. This afternoon's card named 'Cincinnati lose a front-seven starter' as its falsifier; it lost two before the card was even acted on.

case.label: Why Detroit
case.body: FantasyPros rank the Lions DST6 at home to the Jets, and Geno Smith took four sacks last week. The Jets did not practise safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, LB Francisco Mauigoa or TE Mason Taylor on Wednesday. ESPN has Detroit at 7.8, the highest free-agent defence in this file. Detroit's own report has DT Alim McNeill out of practice; The Grey Manes call it short-term.

case.label: The alternatives
case.body: Carolina rank DST2 at Cleveland, but Panthers.com report Devin Lloyd and Jaelan Phillips did not practise Wednesday. The Vikings are free again, but re-adding the unit dropped this morning is the churn this log keeps recording. Detroit is the least damaged of the top six.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Coleman did not practise Wednesday with the ankle; J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey were both limited, per the Denver Gazette. That makes him third in line and explains ESPN's 1.7. He came in by claim on Tuesday, so this reverses a recent move — the exception is that an empty mandatory slot costs more than churn does. Coleman, not Bateman: Bateman is the back-up plan if Zay Flowers sits.

case.label: The collision
case.body: Detroit's opponent is the Jets, and Garrett Wilson starts for you. A good day for the Lions defence usually means a quiet one for Wilson. It's a small cost next to a zero, and Cincinnati had the same problem against Jaylen Warren.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Detroit rule out a second front-seven starter on Friday, or the Jets change quarterback away from Geno Smith. Separately wrong if the Lions finish outside the top 15 defences while Carolina finish top five.

whatWentWrong.title: This afternoon's defence card broke on its own condition within hours
whatWentWrong.lead: The Bengals card said it was wrong if Cincinnati lost a front-seven starter. Wednesday's report ruled out two.

case.label: What happened
case.body: The pick relied on FantasyPros' DST4 rank and on Pittsburgh's last-place offence. It did not check Cincinnati's own injury report, which already had Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill out.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The card at the top is now the Lions. If you already added the Bengals, keep them — don't make a second move to the same seat for about a point.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The Bengals defence finishes top five anyway. That would say interior linemen matter less to a unit against Aaron Rodgers than this correction assumes.

whatWentWrong.title: The empty slot has now survived two briefs
whatWentWrong.lead: It has been empty since 08:37 Wednesday. Every brief that says 'do it Sunday' makes it more likely to still be empty on Sunday.

case.label: The cost
case.body: Zero against roughly seven projected — the biggest single swing on this roster this week, and it is free to fix.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tonight or tomorrow. Nothing is gained by waiting until Friday: none of the remaining Friday reports change which defence is best by more than a point.

worthALook.name: Panthers D/ST
worthALook.lead: The top-ranked free-agent defence, and not the pick because of who missed practice.

case.label: The matchup
case.body: FantasyPros rank Carolina DST2 at Cleveland against Deshaun Watson, projecting 6.94.

case.label: The problem
case.body: Panthers.com: LB Devin Lloyd (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (back) and S Nick Scott (rib) did not practise Wednesday. Lloyd was NFC Defensive Player of the Week.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only if Lloyd and Phillips practise fully on Friday AND Detroit's report gets worse. Otherwise stay with the Lions and don't touch the seat twice.

doNotChase.name: Bengals D/ST
doNotChase.lead: This afternoon's pick, and the market is still buying it.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Two starting defensive tackles out — Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill (CBS). The DST4 ranking was set before the report.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If you already added them, keep them: a second move to the same seat for about a point is the churn this log keeps recording.

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: His quarterback problem is gone. His problem in this league isn't.

case.label: The fact
case.body: CBS report Michael Penix Jr. was a full participant all week and starts Thursday. That removes the quarterback reason for dropping Pitts.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR only, and Likely holds the only tight-end slot. A second tight end has nowhere to play.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely appearing on a Giants injury report.

doNotChase.name: Jaxson Dart
doNotChase.lead: Still the biggest ownership anomaly on this wire, and still nothing.

case.label: The fact
case.body: CBS: out for the season with MCL, PCL and meniscus damage.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. You start Josh Allen in a one-quarterback league.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Two weeks of data is a thin sample. The only needed add is the empty D/ST slot, which the tool doesn't check.
